history.sg_progress: The Office of Information and Communications Technology has completed a comprehensive review of its core services and associated costs, with the primary objectives of: (a) determining the cost of services provided to other United Nations Secretariat entities; (b) establishing a transparent pricing model for each service; and (c) updating service rates. This exercise has resulted in a more accurate and sustainable financial framework that reflects current operational realities and is aligned with best practices as outlined in the cost-recovery policy and guidelines. Three core service rates were approved by the Controller: (a) the United Nations Headquarters core services bundle at $1,156 per user; (b) the peacekeeping core rate at $667 per user; and (c) the non-headquarters/non-field core bundle at $320 per user, applicable to offices away from Headquarters, economic commissions and similar entities. In addition, a rate of $62 for IP telephony services for New York-based users was approved in February 2025. Legacy rates for other on-demand services remain in effect until the newly proposed rates are formally approved.
